title: Invocation session-tag shift causes stale tool responses for rapid-multiplex requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers observed that when they issue high-frequency function/tool invocations (short bursts of concurrent calls that include multipart metadata and session tags) some responses returned content from a previous invocation instead of the expected fresh result. This surfaced across Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private VPC installs, and manifested primarily on edge/proxy paths where requests are multiplexed. Customers reported incorrect structured outputs (stale JSON payloads) and occasional schema mismatches in downstream parsers.
root_cause_summary: A race in the proxy request-correlator triggered incorrect mapping between incoming requests and backend responses when ephemeral request identifiers were truncated for header size optimization. The correlator falls back to a 64-bit session-tag hash for fast-path routing; under high-concurrency bursts this produced collisions/mis-associations with the KV cache attachment step. When a backend response arrived while the correlator still had a pending (but different) request slot marked with the same truncated tag, the response was attached to the wrong invocation. This caused a stale structured tool output to be forwarded and parsed by the client-side parser as if it belonged to the new request.
reproduction_steps: 1) Configure a tool invocation flow that attaches a session tag and uses multipart metadata + small body (common in webhook-style tool calls).
2) From a single tenant send 50-200 concurrent invocations in 100ms bursts to a single edge gateway (repro script attached).
3) Observe responses: some responses contain JSON from a previous invocation ID and parser on client side rejects/accepts wrong schema.
4) Reproduces reliably when request-id header is set to be truncated (edge optimization enabled) and when KV cache attachment occurs within 200ms window of correlated messages.
mitigation: Hotfix rolled to edge correlator: (a) stop truncating request-id for correlation (temporarily always use full 128-bit id), (b) add a short in-memory stabilization window (200ms) to avoid immediate remapping of slots once a request is retired, (c) add a strong assertion that response body JSON's invocation_id matches original invocation header before forwarding. Hotfix deployed to Hosted edge on 2026-03-04 and to Dedicated control-plane within 48h. Private customers were provided configuration and patch instructions for their VPC appliances.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Emergency hotfix to Hosted edge (completed 2026-03-04).
Phase 1: Dedicated control-plane rollout with canary 10% (completed 2026-03-06).
Phase 2: Private/VPC patch release notes + assisted upgrade window with on-prem agents (in progress).
Phase 3: Replace temporary full-id usage with a deterministic collision-resistant tagging scheme and integration tests (scheduled).
monitoring_queries: p99 end-to-end latency for affected tool routes
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Triage call 10:00 UTC. Two paying customers (SaaSCo / DataX) reported this; both on high-throughput ingest path. Assigned to Marco for triage and repro work.

2026-03-02 - Marco Ruiz: Repro script created and pushed to runtime repo. Able to reproduce against staging edge when truncation flag enabled. Initial hypothesis: header truncation collision. Filed small instrument PR to emit full invocation_id in logs.
2026-03-03 - Priya Nair (Support): Customer observed 8/1000 requests returned stale payloads; affected endpoints are tool-runner v2 and webhook gateway. Customers requested urgency and rollback plan.

2026-03-04 - Marco Ruiz: Hotfix deployed to Hosted edge; assertion added to drop responses when invocation_id mismatch detected to avoid forwarding stale payloads. Temporary increase in 99th latency (~6ms) observed but acceptable. Customers confirmed reduced failures.
2026-03-06 - SRE (John Lee): Dedicated rollout canary at 10% passed for 48h. No misassociation events. Promoted to 100% for Dedicated control-plane.
2026-03-09 - Compliance (Marta Gomez): Private/VPC patch validated in partner lab; provided upgrade instructions and a one-click patch script for customers with offline approval process.

2026-03-11 - Design review (Lena Cho): Need UX messaging in Console: surface 'tool invocation integrity' alerts per-route and ability to pause hot-path optimization. Created ticket in Console backlog.

2026-03-12 - Marco Ruiz: Root-cause analysis updated. Next steps: implement collision-resistant tag scheme, add regression E2E tests in CI simulating bursts, and schedule postmortem with customers. Assigned follow-up tickets ENG-110214 (tag-scheme design) and ENG-110215 (e2e regression test harness).
